newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Widow of Albania's Hoxha radiant on jail release.
newsitem.headline: Widow of Albania's Hoxha radiant on jail release.

text.p: Nexhmije Hoxha, widow of the late Albanian Stalinist dictator Enver Hoxha, left jail on Friday looking dignified and unscathed after serving five years in prison for embezzling state cash to fund her luxury lifestyle.

Wearing a long grey coat and yellow woollen scarf the grey-haired Hoxha, 76, looked radiant as she kissed and embraced her two sons and nephew who met her at the gates of Tirana's top-security prison.
The tall widow smiled as she broke off from her family reunion to talk to reporters and pose for photographers.
"I am very pleased to be among free people. But that pleasure is mixed with emotions, anxiety. I am now rushing off to see my children and family," she said.
During Enver Hoxha's iron rule in Europe's poorest and most isolated state, his relatives held high-ranking posts and enjoyed privileges of which ordinary Albanians could only dream.
Hoxha ruled for four decades until his death in April 1985. A popular uprising toppled Albanian communism in December 1990.

His widow was arrested in December 1991 and sentenced to nine years in jail in 1993 on charges of misappropriation of state funds and abuse of power. An appeals court later increased her term to 11 years, a decision upheld by a three-member Supreme Court panel.
Her sentence was reduced three times on the orders of conservative President Sali Berisha and she won a further reduction after a new Penal Code came into effect in 1995.
When Enver Hoxha ruled, the couple lived in a large villa in Tirana guarded around the clock by soldiers. Nexhmije drove her own Fiat saloon car, which is now owned by the defence ministry.
She said on Friday an early priority was to visit the new grave of her husband, first buried in the Martyrs of the Nation cemetery but exhumed in 1992 and reburied in a public plot.
"I do not know where Enver's grave is and I will go and find it. During these five years my mind has not been separated from his name and memories," she said.
Hoxha said she wanted first to spend time with her children but hoped later to publish her memoirs which she wrote in jail.
Most Albanians, facing the challenges of a fledgling market economy, showed little interest in the Hoxha family saga.
"It is good she is out as she was so old," an old woman in the capital said.
"She was at the head of that clan which ruled Albania for half a century. But still I think it was a political trial with her," said a middle-aged man named Kadri.

The Hoxha family has been involved in several legal tussles and, besides Nexhmije, Ilir, her eldest son, was imprisoned in 1995 for one year for inciting hatred after publicly denouncing ruling Democratic Party leaders.
Hoxha's son-in-law Klement Kolaneci was also arrested last October after Albanian police busted what they called a guerrilla organisation of former secret police. "His arrest was absurd," Hoxha said.
The well-heeled widow, once the second most powerful person in Albania, said she had nowhere to go now.
"I don't know where I'm going to live because I have no home," Hoxha said.
